Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for India's reply. Aiden Markram leads his men out onto the park. They are followed by the two Indian openers, Shubman Gill and Abhishek Sharma. Lungi Ngidi will kickstart proceedings with the new ball. Ngidi to Abhishek. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

However, Arshdeep and Bumrah both struggled miserably in the dewy conditions, with their yorkers repeatedly going wrong. David Miller and Donovan Ferreira cashed in brilliantly at the end, stitching together a 23-ball 53-run stand that gave the Proteas a powerful finish. 49 runs came off the final 3 overs that propelled the tourists to 213. India’s highest successful chase in T20Is is 209, and on a true surface like this, they certainly have the resources to gun down the target. As for South Africa, they will have to use their smarts with the ball. Bowling into the surface and taking pace off seems to be the way to go. Back in a bit for the chase.

In search of a breakthrough, Suryakumar Yadav turned to Arshdeep Singh. After an ineffective Powerplay spell, Arshdeep struggled even more on his return, conceding 7 wides in an 18-run over that took him 13 balls to complete. That left Suryakumar scratching his head for answers as Quinton continued to motor along. India found an opening with the wickets of de Kock and Dewald Brevis heading into the death overs, which allowed them to squeeze in a couple of quiet overs.

A solid batting effort from the Proteas, and they will be quite pleased with what they have ended up with. India left much to be desired with the ball, and they were made to pay for it. Having been asked to bat first, Quinton de Kock got off the blocks quickly and powered South Africa to a rapid start, with 53 runs coming in the Powerplay. In the middle phase, Aiden Markram did consume a few dot balls and wasn’t as fluent as his partner, but de Kock remained unfazed and kept the innings moving at a healthy tempo.

OUT! RUN OUT! A superb piece of keeping, and India finally gets the big fish. Something special was needed to get QDK out, and Jitesh Sharma has provided it. Varun Chakaravarthy floats this up, short and around off, Quinton de Kock tries to steer it away but chops it down on the pitch as the ball bounces backwards. De Kock sets off for the run, thinking the ball has gone behind the keeper. However, Jitesh Sharma claws it out with his left hand and then grabs it with his right to break the stumps in a flash. QDK is not sure, and the decision is sent upstairs. The replay shows that the batter is short of his crease. Quinton de Kock departs for a brilliant 90 off 46, and just misses out on a hundred.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! This has been a strong start from South Africa, and the launchpad is well set with plenty of batting still to come. Quinton de Kock has looked a million dollars, while Aiden Markram hasn’t quite found his rhythm yet. His role for now will be to keep the strike rotating and avoid dot balls, an area he has been guilty of slipping into so far. India, meanwhile, haven’t been at their best with the ball. On this surface, the quicker you bowl, the quicker it goes, and the South African batters have made good use of that. The Indian quicks will need to be smarter with their variations going forward. Also, Arshdeep Singh to bowl after the break.

Commentary.Commentary: JUST SHORT! Hardik Pandya tries the yorker but ends up serving a low full toss, on middle. Quinton de Kock picks it up and whips it away but fails to keep it down. It flies towards deep mid-wicket, where Abhishek Sharma runs forward and dives for the catch but the ball just bounces in front of him and gets parried away off his body. Two taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Hardik Pandya to Quinton de Kock, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it away this time! Hardik Pandya lands this short of a length and outside off again. Quinton de Kock uses the width on offer and punches it sweetly through extra cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Hardik Pandya to Quinton de Kock, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and outside off, Quinton de Kock steps across to guide it away but fails to beat backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Hardik Pandya to Quinton de Kock, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full again and on middle, Aiden Markram eases it towards long on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Hardik Pandya to Aiden Markram, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A slower one, full and on middle, Aiden Markram drills it down the pitch. Hardik Pandya tries to get a hand on it on the followthrough but fails to do so as the ball crashes into the stumps at the non-striker's end and goes nowhere.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Hardik Pandya to Aiden Markram, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker, full and on the pads, Quinton de Kock clips it away but straight to square leg. South Africa are 53/1 at the end of the Powerplay.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Axar Patel to Quinton de Kock, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Fires one full but down the leg side, Quinton de Kock leaves it alone. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Axar Patel to Quinton de Kock, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Into the stands! Axar Patel continues to bowl short, this one is on middle and off. Quinton de Kock picks up the length early, moves back and opens up his body. He connects it right from the middle of the bat and whacks it over the deep square leg fence for his fourth biggie of the game. Also, 50 is up for South Africa.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Axar Patel to Quinton de Kock, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish and on middle, Aiden Markram tucks it towards mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Axar Patel to Aiden Markram, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Put away nicely! Axar Patel drags his length back and outside off. Aiden Markram rocks back, extends his arms and slaps it through covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Axar Patel to Aiden Markram, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on middle, Aiden Markram crouches low to swipe it across the line but gets a bottom edge as the ball rolls towards short fine.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Axar Patel to Aiden Markram, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter, short and around off, Aiden Markram backs away to cut it away but miscues it towards point due to the extra bounce.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Axar Patel to Aiden Markram, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Double change. Spin from both ends now as Axar Patel comes into the attack.

Chance? At 95.2 kph, short and on middle. Markram waits back and pushes out in front of his body. Chakaravarthy gets low to his right on his follow-through and gets a hand on it. A single is taken as the ball goes behind the bowler. Did that carry, though? The look on the face of Varun suggests that it was a chance. We will have to wait for the replays. Oh yes, that was a catching opportunity. It came at shin height, but the bowler could not cling on as he stuck out his right hand.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Varun Chakaravarthy to Aiden Markram, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit too short, on off, Quinton de Kock whips it from the crease to the right of deep mid-wicket. QDK calls for two but Abhishek Sharma is quick in the deep to get around and keeps the batters down to a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Varun Chakaravarthy to Quinton de Kock, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flat and short, on the off pole. Markram punches it down the deck. Varun fails to make the stop to his right and Aiden is off the mark with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Varun Chakaravarthy to Aiden Markram, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and sliding onto the pads, Aiden wrists it off the back foot to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Varun Chakaravarthy to Aiden Markram, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and another googly, on off, Aiden Markram lunges and taps it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Varun Chakaravarthy to Aiden Markram, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Aiden Markram walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! KNOCKED HIM OVER! Varun Chakaravarthy strikes with his very first ball. Googly first up from Varun, short and on middle. Hendricks presses on the back foot and swivels for the pull. The ball skids through to sneak under the blade and crashes into the stumps. Reeza falls for 8 (10). South Africa are 38/1 in 4.1 overs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Varun Chakaravarthy to Reeza Hendricks, OUT! b Varun Chakaravarthy.

Commentary.Commentary: Change? Yes, time for some mystery spin as Varun Chakaravarthy replaces Arshdeep Singh.

SIX! Quinton de Kock looks in the mood tonight! Fractionally short by Bumrah, on middle. Quinton crouches a bit to get under the ball and pivots to unleash the pull. Hits it away from the man at deep square leg to his left for a six. An expensive over from Bumrah. 16 runs off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Jasprit Bumrah to Quinton de Kock, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: A low full toss, on middle, dips a bit on the batter, Reeza Hendricks pushes it to the left of mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Jasprit Bumrah to Reeza Hendricks, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rolls his fingers on the ball, on a short of a length, on middle, Quinton tucks it beside the strip on the leg side and takes a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Jasprit Bumrah to Quinton de Kock, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Two wides! Bumrah spots Reeza backing away and follows him with a quick, short ball. Hendricks tries to take it on but the ball flies past his blade, down leg. The keeper, Jitesh Sharma flings himself to his left and gets a hand on it. The ball is parried away to deep fine leg and the batters cross over for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Jasprit Bumrah to Reeza Hendricks, 2 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Clean strike! Angled in at 141.9 kph, on a back of a length, on middle. This sits up to be hit and Hendricks swivels to pull it over deep square leg for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Jasprit Bumrah to Reeza Hendricks, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Pace taken off, on a length, on off, Hendricks guides it to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Jasprit Bumrah to Reeza Hendricks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bumrah looks to fire it in full but ends up serving a full toss, on middle. It comes at an awkward height and Reeza tugs it to mid-wicket. Hendricks has a look at the square leg umpire but the umpire thinks it is below the waist.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Jasprit Bumrah to Reeza Hendricks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A searing yorker, tailing back in late, at the toes. Reeza Hendricks gets his bat down in time and digs it out in front of mid-wicket for a single to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Arshdeep Singh to Reeza Hendricks, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed across the batter, full in length, Hendricks firms the drive to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Arshdeep Singh to Reeza Hendricks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lands it on a back of a length, on top of off, QDK drops it with soft hands in front of point and gets to the other end quickly.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! That has gone way back into the stands! Neither short nor full, it comes at thigh height to QDK, around the off stump. De Kock is standing out of his crease and he climbs into it. Dispatches the pull over deep square leg for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Missed out! Short and wide on off, begging to be hit. Quinton de Kock extends his hands to go hard on the off side but mistimes it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Put away! Arshdeep goes into the surface, over off. Quinton de Kock rises with the bounce and pulls it off the back foot over mid-wicket. He does not get it from the middle of the bat and the ball teases Shivam Dube all the way through before touching the boundary cushions.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: At 140.2 kph, yorker from Bumrah but a bit too straight, Quinton de Kock tries to tickle it fine but only manages to get a feather on it. The ball deflects off the pads to deep fine leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Jasprit Bumrah to Quinton de Kock, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Very full and wide on off, de Kock reaches out and knocks it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Jasprit Bumrah to Quinton de Kock, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Fuller and leaving the left-hander from over the wicket, Quinton de Kock has a swipe across the line to go big on the leg side but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Jasprit Bumrah to Quinton de Kock, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! On a hard length, a bit of lift off the deck, under the left armpit. Hendricks gets on his toes to help it away but misses. A leg bye is taken as the ball goes off the body behind on the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Jasprit Bumrah to Reeza Hendricks, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! Swinging away, on a length, Reeza pushes out in front with a straight bat and plays for the ball angling into him. This moves away and Hendricks gets beaten past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Jasprit Bumrah to Reeza Hendricks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts with a good-length delivery, around the off stump, Reeza Hendricks presents a straight bat and pushes it towards mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Jasprit Bumrah to Reeza Hendricks, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Jasprit Bumrah to share the attack.
Honing in on the off pole, on a good length, Quinton stabs it down the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! A Quinton de Kock special! Slanting into the pads, on a length, de Kock plays his trademark pick-up shot off the pads. Clears the deep backward square leg fence with ease for the first six of the night.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Quinton de Kock and South Africa are underway! Fuller and moving away in the air, Quinton de Kock goes up and over cover but does not quite get hold of it. Clears the in-field and the ball plugs in the outfield. Tilak Varma gives it a chase and mops it up. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! Short and wide on off, there to be put away, Quinton de Kock stands tall and looks to thrash it through covers. He mistimes the shot wide of cover. QDK takes a few steps down the track and seeing that, Reeza Hendricks also sets off for the run. De Kock sends Reeza back but it is too late by then. Tilak Varma moves to his right, picks the ball up and has a shy at the bowling end but misses. Reeza was gone had the throw hit.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags the length back, on middle, de Kock hangs back and tries to work it away on the leg side with a closed bat face but ends up dropping it at his feet.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shape straight away for Arshdeep! Curving away from the left-hander from over the wicket, on a good length, Quinton de Kock shoulders arms.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Arshdeep Singh to Quinton de Kock, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get underway! The crowd has turned up in big numbers here in Mullanpur for the first-ever men's international at this venue. It's a cold evening, but the energy in the stands is electric. The two umpires now make their way to the middle, and the Indian players follow right behind, fanning out to take their positions on the field. Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks are the two openers for South Africa. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

The skipper of South Africa, Aiden Markram says he would have bowled first as well. He feels it looks like a pretty good wicket to the eye. Shares that there haven’t been many international games played here, but they will look to put a good total on the board and then try to put India under pressure with the ball. Aiden adds that there are always lessons to take from nights like the previous game, but they don’t want to dwell too much on that loss. Markram admits he is not entirely sure what a good total might be on this surface, so getting off to a good start becomes crucial. Informs that they have made three changes from a rotation point of view, with Tristan Stubbs, Keshav Maharaj and Anrich Nortje missing out.

India's captain Suryakumar Yadav says that they will bowl first. Adds that the dew has already started to settle while they were warming up. Mentions that this has been a great ground to play in franchise cricket, but a Women's international game also happened here, which was good, and he is excited as this is the first Men's international game at this ground. Says that everyone must know their responsibility and they batted really well in the last match and reckons 175 was a little above par. Tells that Hardik Pandya was brilliant and gives a nice balance to the team. Further says that the way he bowled was also important as his overs are crucial for the team. Informs that they are unchanged.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (WK), Aiden Markram (C), Reeza Hendricks (In for Tristan Stubbs), Dewald Brevis, David Miller, George Linde (In for Keshav Maharaj), Donovan Ferreira, Marco Jansen, Lutho Sipamla, Lungi Ngidi, Ottneil Baartman (In for Anrich Nortje).

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Abhishek Sharma, Shubman Gill, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Axar Patel, Hardik Pandya, Shivam Dube, Jitesh Sharma (WK), Varun Chakaravarthy, Arshdeep Singh, Jasprit Bumrah.
TOSS - 'Tails' is the call from Aiden Markram, but it has come down as a head. India have elected to BOWL first.

The Punjab Cricket Association has inaugurated the Yuvraj Singh Stand here at the stadium, and the man himself is now addressing the Indian huddle. A stand has also been inaugurated in honour of World Cup-winning captain, Harmanpreet Kaur, who also hails from this very region.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta is pitchside. He informs that it is a cold winter evening in New Chandigarh. Deep points out that the square boundaries are 68 metres on either side, with 73 metres straight down the ground. Feels this is a much better wicket to bat on as compared to Cuttack. Pommie Mbangwa agrees with Deep. He notes that the surface looks compact and carries a bit of sheen. Adds that there are a few cracks, but the grass covering is nice and even right across the wicket. Mentions that your knuckles hurt when you tap on the pitch, which tells you it is firm. He also likes that it is a big ground and that the pitch is right in the centre, meaning batters won’t get away with a mishit. Pommie shares that the average winning score here in T20s is around 180. Deep does not expect the cracks to open up, and he anticipates a high-scoring game.

This is the first men’s international at this venue, but it is not entirely an unknown entity. A couple of women’s ODIs between India and Australia were played here in September, the first of which was particularly high scoring. IPL games have also been staged here over the past couple of seasons. Of the 5 night games earlier this year, 4 were won by the side batting first. However, considering the time of the year and the likelihood of dew, the captain winning the toss may still prefer to chase. Stick around for the toss and team news.

On the other hand, South Africa must regroup quickly after being bowled out for just 74, their lowest T20I total. Like India, they too have key players searching for form, most notably captain Aiden Markram and Quinton de Kock. De Kock is yet to make much of an impact since returning to the T20I setup, and Markram has gone more than three years without a fifty in the format. To their credit, the Proteas pacers quickly adapted to what was a sticky surface in Cuttack, but they lost control at the death against Hardik Pandya and will be keen to tighten that aspect of their game.

For India, Hardik Pandya’s rescue act in the opener underlined just how important he is to this side and the value he brings in pressure situations. The lack of runs from skipper Suryakumar Yadav and his deputy Shubman Gill, however, remains a concern, with both having gone more than a year without a fifty in the format. With the ball, the hosts hit all the right notes and barely put a foot wrong. A collective batting effort will be on their agenda as they look to carry that rhythm forward and extend the lead.

Hello, one and all! From Cuttack, we have moved up north as the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in Mullanpur plays host to the second T20I. India have landed the first punch in this five-round bout, and with a quick turnaround between games, South Africa will need to produce a strong response to draw level in the series.
... MATCH DAY ...

The focus of the five-match T20I series shifts to the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in Mullanpur, New Chandigarh, for the second encounter. This match is a crucial fixture, particularly for the visiting South Africa side, which is now trailing 1-0 after a crushing defeat in the series opener. India enter the second T20I with massive momentum following a dominant 101-run victory in Cuttack, where they successfully defended a total of 175. The performance was a testament to the team's depth and the impactful return of key all-rounder Hardik Pandya. Pandya's blistering 59 off 28 balls single-handedly propelled India to a competitive total on a sticky wicket, and his contribution with the ball underlined his value to the side. India’s bowling unit was also exceptional, skittling South Africa for a historic low T20I total of just 74. The spinners, including the world's No. 1 T20I bowler Varun Chakaravarthy, alongside the disciplined pace of Jasprit Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh, were relentless. Despite the commanding win, the focus will remain on captain Suryakumar Yadav and vice-captain Shubman Gill. Both players are under scrutiny for a prolonged lean patch in the T20I format. For Aiden Markram's South Africa, the second T20I is a do-or-die scenario to prevent the series from quickly slipping away. The visitors' batting lineup collapsed spectacularly in the opener, highlighting serious issues with their approach on turning tracks. The dismissals of key batters like Quinton de Kock, Tristan Stubbs, David Miller, and Markram himself in quick succession signaled a lack of ability to adapt to the challenging pitch conditions and the senior players simply need to step up. Young power-hitter Dewald Brevis is an important player in the middle order who can turn the game on its head if he gets going on a truer surface. South Africa possesses a formidable pace battery, including Marco Jansen and Lungi Ngidi. They will need to exploit the early assistance on offer at the new venue and put pressure on the Indian top order, who have shown occasional vulnerability. The surface at Mullanpur is generally known to offer even bounce with a quick outfield, often encouraging free stroke play. There is typically early assistance for seamers, making the powerplay a crucial phase but as the game goes on, the spinners will also have a role to play. Given the evening start and the possibility of dew, the captain winning the toss will likely elect to bowl first, a traditional preference in Indian T20 matches. Who are you backing for the win?
